newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end weak on renewed rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end weak on renewed rate worries.

text.p: Renewed fears about rising interest rates pushed Hong Kong stocks to a weaker close on Tuesday, with investors prompted to take profits after recent gains following a rise in the U.S. long bond yield.
The Hang Seng index closed 85.71 points lower at 11,338.93. Turnover was HK$3.50 billion compared to HK$4.93 billion on Friday. The market was closed on Monday for Liberation Day.
"The equity markets are moving with the bond market," said Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel.
The U.S. long bond shed 18/32 on Monday, pushing the yield to its highest level in almost four weeks at 7.00 percent.
The minutes of the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee's July 2-3 meeting, released on Friday, revived fears of higher interest rates. The Dow industrials fell 28.85 points overnight to 5,693.89.

"U.S. interest rate trends still have some impact on the Hong Kong market and also the market went up quite strongly over the last two weeks so there is some profit-taking," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
The Hang Seng index rose 2.2 percent last week.
Property stocks were weak. Cheung Kong fell HK$0.50 to HK$56.25 and Henderson Land slipped HK$0.25 to HK$61.00.

Hutchison Whampoa fell HK$1.20 to HK$47.00, still smarting from the release of lower-than-expected interim results last week. Traders said news that Hutchison's Subic Bay project was under review by the Philippine government also hurt the shares.

A legal adviser to Philippine President Fidel Ramos said Ramos has stepped into a row over the Subic Bay project after International Container Terminal Services Inc appealed to Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority to reverse its decision to award the port contract to Hutchison.
The H-share index ended the session 17.38 points lower at 825.75.
Shares in Shanghai Petrochemical dropped HK$0.175 to HK$2.075 after it announced plans to place shares in the United States and Canada.
Yizheng Chemical fell HK$0.06 to HK$1.74 following a drop in its first-half net profit to 212.00 million yuan from 836.13 million in the same period last year.

Another H-share company, Dongfang Electrical, also fell after its interim earnings. The company posted interim profit of 28.36 million yuan, down from 34.36 million yuan, and its shares fell HK$0.025 to HK$2.40.
